cells.tense: You are standing at the wheel right now, and the course you set is holding.
cells.act: surrender the outcome and keep the act
cells.ask: Take something you're growing and name the part that isn't yours to steer. Keep doing the work. Just know which part you don't decide.
cells.core:
You've picked a direction and you're keeping it fed, and holding it steady isn't draining you. That's rarer than it sounds. The care runs alongside the aim instead of against it — you can stand over a thing without gripping it, and it still gets what it needs.

Look at what you're growing and find the edge of what you actually steer. Not the whole thing. One edge. Say the shape of that to yourself plainly, so your effort stops going into the part that isn't yours to push. The grip you keep there doesn't make it grow faster. What stays in your hands afterward is real work, and you'll know it by how it settles you.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold a direction without forcing what grows in it.
cells.verb: tending what is growing, without forcing its shape
cells.place: at the point where direction is chosen and held

cells.tense: You will reach for the outcome and try to write it before it is ready to be written.
cells.act: let the path show itself instead of forcing clarity
cells.ask: Pick what you're growing. For a week, do only the work today actually needs — no course corrections, no fixing tomorrow. Let the next stretch show itself.
cells.core:
There's something you're growing, and the picture of how it turns out is gripping you. You keep reaching in — setting direction, correcting, hovering — certain that if you stop stewing, it goes wrong. The concern is genuine. It's landing as pressure, and the thing you're tending can feel the weight of your future on it.

For a week, give it only the work today needs. Not less care — today's care. Let the next steps come up out of what's already there instead of out of your worry about where it has to land. If you can picture how it turns out from what you've actually lived with it, let the picture come. If you can't, let the week be plain. Steer what's here now. The road does most of it.

cells.tense: Nothing has grown near you in a long while, and you stand at a door already behind you.
cells.act: pick the one you would be sorriest to lose
cells.ask: Look at what you're growing right now, and choose the piece you'd mourn if it went. Turn toward it. When you catch yourself forsaking it, come back. That's the whole thing.
cells.core:
Nothing has gotten near you in a while. Not that you're careless — you've gone quiet around what you tend. Some of it slipped away before you noticed. From where you sit it reads as being fine on your own, and from outside it reads as something that has been holding still.

Find the piece you'd mourn if it went. Not the piece that needs you most — the piece that would wound you to let go. Stand next to it and stay a while. You don't have to feel inspired to do it. You just have to bring your attention back when it wanders, and it will wander. That's not a sign you've stopped caring. It's the work of the thing, and it's small enough to do today.
cells.sheetLine: The piece you'd mourn is where you come back.

cells.tense: You are carrying care you never chose, and the carrying is going on now.
cells.act: stop holding what no longer serves
cells.ask: Find what you're holding out of habit. Not everything — one. Set it down for a week and don't pick it back up. When the urge to take it arrives, let it pass.
cells.core:
Care is happening, and you'd say it's just what the situation calls for. The ones close to you experience you as the steady one. Both are true at once, and the part you leave out of your own account is the hand doing the work.

Start by seeing the care as something you do, not as how things happen to be. Then choose one thing you're holding and set it down for a week, on purpose. If guilt arrives, let it arrive without taking the thing back — it can be an alarm bell, not a command. If nothing else holds it, that tells you something. The grip you keep on everything is not what makes you the one who cares.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is 'some of them will stay well on less from you' — the record shows the balance feeding toward Release, but it does not show any handoff to other people. A reader could reasonably say the capacities listed are capacities, not arrangements, and that no one else's side is in the draw. The asks do survive a wrong read: no ask requires another person to be present, and no ask ties itself to a feeling the person may not have. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is the one about other hands picking up what was carried — cut it.

A reader could reasonably say this is simply a person who is good at caretaking and doesn't mind, and that objection stands; the ask still works for them, since noticing the act as a doing costs nothing and can be refused. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person was 'the hand doing the work' — a picture that flattered the writer, so it is gone. I also watch 'never' and 'every' and have replaced the universal with the card's actual scope.
